articles.title_orig: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in 2025, launches internal probe over China chip claims
articles.title_zh: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in 2025, launches internal probe over China chip claims
articles.content_orig:
Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed announced on Sunday that it has initiated an internal investigation into allegations that advanced Nvidia chips were diverted to China in violation of US export restrictions, CNBC reported.
In an emailed statement to CNBC, Megaspeed rejected recent reporting regarding its operations as lacking "verifiable evidence" and said it has retained external legal counsel to conduct a "thorough internal investigation."
The company also moved to distance itself from former executive Alice Huang, asserting that she "officially left Megaspeed effective August 30, 2025 and currently has no role with the Company," while declining to comment on her private affairs.
Operating across Singapore and Indonesia as a self-described "core business partner" renting out Nvidia graphics processing unit computing power, Megaspeed maintained that its global supply-chain controls comply strictly with "United States export control requirements and local jurisdiction rules" in every market where it operates.
The company added that it will review the media reporting and update stakeholders as appropriate.
The scrutiny follows the Nov. 12 resignation of Nvidia co-founder and Chief Executive Jensen Huang, who stepped down after leading the US chipmaker for more than three decades. His exit came after he acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife following reports linking him to a woman sources identified to CBS News as Alice Huang.
According to The New York Times, US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang is a Chinese intelligence asset, while CNBC reported she owned stakes in Chinese businesses that benefited sanctioned telecommunications giant Huawei during her affair with the former Nvidia chief.
Singaporean authorities previously confiscated Alice Huang's passport in June 2025, restricting her international travel for eight months while seeking US assistance over alleged chip shipments to China, according to US media reports.

articles.title_orig: Bessent Says Nvidia Needs ‘Dramatic Shakeup’ After Huang Ouster
articles.title_zh: Bessent Says Nvidia Needs ‘Dramatic Shakeup’ After Huang Ouster
articles.content_orig:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang 's resignation, questioning whether the chipmaker pursued illicit sales of its advanced artificial intelligence chips to boost earnings.
Bessent said Nvidia's board should look outside the company for its next chief executive and suggested other executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with U.S. export controls.
"I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent said in an interview on Fox News.
The remarks come as Bessent has stepped up his criticism of Nvidia and amid a growing feud with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's department over the suspected diversion of advanced AI chips to China, all while defending President Donald Trump's handling of the matter.
Huang resigned Thursday following revelations about his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed , whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of spying for China. Megaspeed is suspected of diverting Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls.
Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO.
Bessent suggested Sunday that Nvidia's problems extended well beyond Huang.
"If this were a bank and they hadn't complied like this, the OCC would be in there right now, and a lot of the executives would be removed," Bessent said, referring to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.
Bessent also questioned Nvidia's financial disclosures, pointing to a surge in reported Singapore revenue as its China sales fell.
Nvidia stopped separately reporting Singapore revenue in November 2025, saying a new methodology based on customers' headquarters rather than billing addresses better reflected the geographic distribution of its sales.
Bessent's remarks came two days after he told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that several federal agencies had supported adding Megaspeed to the government's export blacklist for months.
"But Commerce has the pen," Bessent said.
The public rebuke followed reporting by Axios that Bessent confronted Lutnick in the White House Situation Room over Commerce's failure to act against Megaspeed. Commerce denied that the confrontation took place.
Lutnick is also facing scrutiny over his family's financial ties to Nvidia. CNBC reported Friday that Cantor Fitzgerald, the Wall Street firm formerly run by Lutnick and now led by his sons, has helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for Nvidia's business partners.
Cantor said Nvidia share holdings fell nearly 50% over six months as national security concerns surrounding Huang escalated. The positions were associated with client swap transactions, not proprietary investments, the investment bank said.
There is no evidence Lutnick shared sensitive information with his sons or that Cantor traded on such information.
Bessent on Sunday said Trump had drawn a firm line against sales of chips more advanced than Nvidia's H200 to China . Trump himself authorized H200 sales to approved Chinese customers in December —following months of lobbying by Huang — in an arrangement under which the U.S. government would receive a 25% cut.
Bessent's latest criticism comes two days before Nvidia is scheduled to report its first quarterly earnings since Huang's departure.

articles.title_zh: Trump to meet Xi, Putin in China for nuclear arms talks; Ukraine off agenda

SEOUL — President Trump will get his wish for a historic meeting among the three most powerful men in the world — Xi Jinping of China, Vladimir Putin of Russia and himself — at a summit Thursday in southern China.
But Moscow, Beijing and Washington already know their leaders are arriving at the Shenzhen conference with disparate aims.
Trump hopes to focus the meeting on nuclear nonproliferation, urging the Russian and Chinese presidents to work with him to scale back the world’s largest nuclear stockpiles. Putin pressed for the meeting to discuss his ongoing war in Ukraine . And Xi wants to discuss neither, only embracing the idea of the summit to show the world China can help broker peace on the international stage, Chinese officials told The Times.
“That’ll be interesting,” Trump said earlier this week,  teasing the trilateral summit before the White House formally confirmed the meeting Friday.
“We’re talking a lot of things, including denuclearization,” he added, “but we’ll be talking a lot of things.”
U.S. officials have acknowledged they do not expect the meeting to result in a breakthrough on arms control. China is openly racing to build up its nuclear capacity — a nonnegotiable policy in Beijing, which sees its arsenal dwarfed by an American stockpile nearly 10 times the size.
“We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement. I would characterize this as the entry point,” one senior Trump administration official said. “This is the beginning of hopefully a conversation that can be productive going forward.”
Trump’s break from long-standing tradition in U.S.-Russia relations was real, but it should not have been entirely surprising.
The Chinese, too, threw cold water on the chances of a breakthrough, with one Chinese official telling The Times the central government saw no benefit to a pause.
“It is a matter of survival,” the official said.
The United States and Russia still command the world’s two dominant nuclear arsenals, with over 5,000 warheads each. China has an estimated 620 — but in catching up, it is developing new warheads with more sophisticated delivery systems.
Moscow, too, is modernizing its weapons, after the Trump administration allowed the last major U.S.-Russian nuclear arms treaty to expire earlier this year.
Though expectations are low for a nuclear breakthrough, Trump doesn’t want to discuss Putin’s priorities, either, the U.S. official added.
“He does not intend to talk about Ukraine in that meeting,” the official said. “China is not really part of that track, so it doesn’t really seem appropriate.”
Ukraine has grown increasingly concerned by Trump’s pressure campaign to force it into concessions to Moscow as he pushes to end the war.
The Trump administration has brought Russian and Ukrainian officials together at a working level to explore the viability of peace talks. But a long-standing U.S. policy on the war — not to negotiate about Ukraine without Ukraine — could be further compromised at a trilateral with Putin and Xi.
The only American business leader confirmed to join Trump in Asia is Elon Musk, the Tesla and SpaceX chief who was seen as instrumental in the decision last month to restrict Ukraine’s access on the battlefield to Starlink , the satellite internet service owned by Musk.
Beijing has struck a careful balance on Ukraine, publicly issuing its respect for sovereign borders — a position popular among Chinese voices who support Kyiv — while giving Moscow diplomatic cover, an economic lifeline and technological support throughout the war.
The summit’s stark lack of substance surprised even the closest China watchers.
Their competing agendas could make the summit little more than a spectacle, yet still produce images that hark back to the famous Yalta Conference — held in Crimea, the Ukrainian peninsula currently occupied by Russia, in 1945 — where Josef Stalin, Franklin Delano Roosevelt and Winston Churchill carved up a postwar order.
The summit on Chinese soil offers Xi a powerful image to broadcast worldwide , demonstrating an emergent superpower can bring together the leaders of two historic rivals in the name of peace.
Putin gets to present himself as a global player, despite the devastation wrought on Russia’s economy and military standing after four bruising years of war.
And it allows Trump to reassert his global relevance after this month’s midterms delivered the worst electoral rebuke to a president in half a century, rivaling the backlash against President Nixon during Watergate.

articles.title_zh: Israel kidnapped Iranian generals, killed one, in effort to locate Ron Arad — NYT

At a protest in 2025 in Tel Aviv, supporters of Israeli hostages held captive by Hamas held pictures of the hostages and of Ron Arad, who has been missing since 1986. Credit... Itai Ron/Reuters
By Adam Goldman Ronen Bergman Farnaz Fassihi and Hwaida Saad
Ronen Bergman, Farnaz Fassihi, Adam Goldman and Hwaida Saad have spent years investigating the disappearance of the Israeli airman Ron Arad.
Gen. Abdullah Saberi, an Iranian commander, stepped out for a jog early one morning in an upscale diplomatic quarter of Syria’s capital. Israeli intelligence officers waited nearby. Posing as movers, they had slipped past the neighborhood’s security checkpoints.
As he headed for a nearby park, General Saberi passed two men who carried an oversize refrigerator box. In a flash, the men restrained the general, drugged him, threw the box over his head, shoved him into a white van and left as if nothing had happened.
He was whisked to Israel for interrogation, according to numerous officials in the Middle East, including senior Iranian officials close to General Saberi and a Syrian official who reviewed video of the September 2021 kidnapping.
As a veteran of Iran’s powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, General Saberi knew many secrets. But his interrogators were interested in only one.
What did he know about Ron Arad?
Mr. Arad, an Israeli airman, vanished decades ago, and the Israeli military says he is the only service member classified as missing in action. The government’s long search for him has captivated the public and has come to symbolize Israel’s commitment, rooted in Jewish tradition , to bringing its soldiers home, dead or alive. Articles, books and documentaries have been produced about the hunt for Mr. Arad.
The Israeli government was so determined to find him that, even four decades after his disappearance, it took the risk of kidnapping General Saberi in the shadow of his own embassy.

articles.title_orig: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
articles.title_zh: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
articles.content_orig:
Alice Huang, a suspected China spy who has been linked to Nvidia's former boss Jensen Huang, left her executive role at Megaspeed in August last year, the  company says.
Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of the AI chip-making giant Nvidia after it emerged he had allegedly had affairs with Alice Huang as well as with one of his employees.
Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in south-east Asia and the scandal at Nvidia has raised questions about the possibility that high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.
It said it was aware of reports "containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence".
It added that it "conducts legitimate and lawful business" and has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation".
On Friday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed fellow Trump cabinet colleague Howard Lutnick's commerce department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-end chips.
Bessent told CNBC that several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months... but Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process".
The so-called entity list restricts US trade with overseas firms and individuals.
Lutnick has been called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over his department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.
Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Jensen Huang.
Megaspeed is suspected of giving backdoor access to Nvidia chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
Nvidia has been banned from selling its advanced chips to China.
While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.
Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations.
Megaspeed said it "designs and maintains its global operational and supply-chain control frameworks to comply with all applicable laws and regulatory regimes". It said this includes "US export control requirements and local jurisdiction rules in every market where we operate".
China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.

articles.title_orig: Trump heads to Asia with hopes of shifting the momentum after midterm setbacks hurt him at home
articles.title_zh: Trump heads to Asia with hopes of shifting the momentum after midterm setbacks hurt him at home
articles.content_orig:
Tussle for influence as trade, tech and regional security to take centre stage in China, Philippines and Cambodia meetings
World leaders will fly in to Asia for back-to-back high-level summits this week against the backdrop of the tussle for influence between the superpowers China and the US.
Beijing will have the home advantage when it welcomes Donald Trump to its southern technology hub of Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) leaders’ meeting. It starts two weeks after the US leader lost midterm elections .
The summit also comes after an awkward-at-best revelation that the head of Nvidia, the US chipmaker that for a long time was the world’s most valuable company, was having an affair with a woman US intelligence suspects was a Chinese spy .
Apec represents more than 60% of global GDP and has primarily promoted free trade and multilateralism. This year’s meeting could be defined, however, by the confirmed trilateral meeting between Trump, the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin of Russia.
The three-way meeting has been likened to a modern-day Yalta, when in 1945 then US president, Franklin D Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and the Soviet leader Joseph Stalin met in Crimea to carve up Europe after the second world war. However, analysts say a “Yalta 2.0” that issues edicts on Ukraine and Taiwan without their involvement is unlikely.
Xiaoyu Pu, an associate professor at the University of Nevada’s department of political science, said a three-way meeting “might be more symbolic than substantive, although symbolism itself matters in great-power diplomacy.
“Trump appears interested in nuclear arms control and denuclearisation. Xi’s priority is likely to maintain a stable relationship with Washington while preserving China’s strategic partnership with Russia. Putin, meanwhile, wants to maintain his bargaining leverage over Ukraine.”
Apec begins on Wednesday and follows a flurry of other diplomatic gatherings, chief among them the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) meeting in the Philippines , starting on Sunday, which Trump will attend.
While he is in Manila, US officials will hold a sidelines meeting of the so-called Quad – Australia, India, Japan and the US. In addition, a Francophone summit, which includes the Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, and the French president, Emmanuel Macron, is happening concurrently in Cambodia.
Critical global issues at all these summits will include AI supply chains and governance, tariff reductions and the green energy transition. Trump’s focus has been on denuclearisation. A key regional focus will be on the South China Sea , where Beijing has built massive military outposts in disputed waters, as well as the gigantic Indonesian forest fire haze blanketing the region.
The humanitarian and security crisis in Myanmar has become a perennial issue, as is status of Taiwan, which China does not recognise. The self-ruled island is sending the founder of the tech hardware company Acer as its envoy to Apec.
For well over a decade, Washington’s engagement in the region has been coloured by concern over the rise of China, with the then president Barack Obama telling Australia’s parliament in 2011 that the US was “a Pacific power, and we are here to stay” – a policy known as the “pivot to Asia”.
The strategy of intense diplomacy and trade deals was adopted by Joe Biden, who hoped to gather allies on the continent who wanted to balance their relationships with both superpowers.
Some analysts see Trump’s transactional style in Asia as a continuation of the pivot policy. Still, the president’s volatility and unpredictability have spooked smaller nations, who regard China as a more predictable partner.
Jayant Menon, an economist at Singapore’s Iseas-Yusof Ishak Institute, said that countries in south-east Asia had been “laying the groundwork for a future with reduced dependence on the United States” by seeking deals elsewhere, including with each other and the EU.
“Amid persistent uncertainty and an administration determined to levy tariffs by any legal means, south-east Asia’s ability to ride out another round of tariffs depends on deeper regional integration and diversification beyond the US market,” he wrote this month in the East Asia Forum.
Beijing’s more predictable policies do not necessarily make it any more palatable for its regional neighbours, however, and the Chinese premier, Li Qiang, could have tough talks when he goes to Manila for the Asean summit, especially on the South China Sea.
China’s top diplomat, Wang Yi, recently urged Manila to rein in Filipino politicians who he said had repeatedly “smeared” Beijing, after public outcries in the country over the disputed waters.
Brunei, China, Malaysia, the Philippines, Taiwan and Vietnam have been locked in decades-long territorial standoffs in the busy waterway, which could sit on deposits of oil and gas . Washington has sent military ships on “freedom of navigation operations”, despite Chinese outcries, although US-linked crises in Iran, Ukraine, Venezuela, and Palestine and Israel have sucked up Washington’s focus under Trump’s second term.
A decades-long attempt to sign a South China Sea pact is not expected to happen at this year’s Asean summit, as previously hoped. Despite monthly meetings, negotiations will have to continue next year, when Asean’s leadership rotates to Singapore .
Diplomats at the Asean summit will also be focusing on Myanmar, which is seeking reintegration . Each country in the group is assessing how to deal with their isolated neighbour. The timing of summits this week coincides with a judgment in the international court of justice on Thursday that could find Myanmar responsible for genocide. The coup leader, Min Aung Hlaing, remains barred from Asean but is allowed to send a representative.
Asia’s week of diplomacy will be followed next month by the G20 summit in Miami, Florida, which Xi is expected to attend if US and Chinese relations continue to hold steady.

articles.title_orig: 9 Fast Food Chains With The Highest Quality Beef Burgers
articles.title_zh: 9 Fast Food Chains With The Highest Quality Beef Burgers
articles.content_orig:
Quality isn't necessarily the first thing that comes to mind when we think of fast food. It's something that we'll compromise on for convenience, speed, and affordability. But as fast food has become increasingly expensive, and a growing number of people feel that some iconic fast food items have gone downhill , customers have more reason to question what they're getting for their hard-earned cash.
There are a handful of fast-food chains that understand this — some are well-known brands, while others you may never have heard of. Their commitment doesn't just include what happens in the kitchen. It starts with the beef itself, and some even work directly with ranchers and farmers to ensure it meets particular standards. To build this list, we looked at four markers of quality: transparency regarding where the beef comes from, how the cattle are raised, whether the patties are ever frozen, and how the burgers are prepared.
Quality assurance and ethical sourcing are at the forefront of the Wendy's ethos, from the fresh, never-frozen 100% beef patties to its Animal Care Standards Program. The chain's website covers various areas of its sourcing process, including its beef supply chain, a commitment to eliminating the routine use of medically important antibiotics by 2030, and various sustainable practices. The site also addresses its investment in improving livestock conditions and exclusive use of beef from Beef Quality Assurance-certified sources. Suffice it to say, Wendy's offers more transparency than many fast-food chains.
Even the square shape of the burger was inspired by the idea of quality. Founder Dave Thomas wanted the patties to hang over the bun so that the quality of the beef was visible before the first bite. The patties contain zero fillers or additives and are transported from processing facilities to restaurants in refrigerated trucks. Once the patties arrive, every Wendy's burger is made to order on a grill and served fresh and juicy to customers.
With fewer than 500 locations across the U.S., In-N-Out is not as widespread as other fast-food chains. A major reason for that is its staunch commitment to quality. The chain follows a strict policy of no freezers, no pre-packaging, and no microwaves for its beef patties. As a result, it can only make its patties at certain facilities and only opens stores in locations that are within a certain distance of its distribution outposts. Also, unlike many chains, it refuses to franchise and instead prefers to remain privately owned.
As for where In-N-Out actually gets its beef , our sources indicate that most of it comes from a California-based supplier called Harris Ranch. It's one of the largest beef suppliers in the Western United States, and it says its cattle are grass-raised and grain-finished. That said, it only supplies the meat. In-N-Out handles the inspection, removes the bones, and grinds the beef used for each patty, which it grills fresh for every order. The chain says the patties are made from 100% USDA ground chuck and are free of additives, fillers, and preservatives.
An up-and-coming East Coast chain, 7th Street Burger has exploded in popularity since opening in 2021. It keeps its menu short and sweet, offering only a cheeseburger, a double cheeseburger, a vegetarian-friendly option with Impossible Meat, and fries. The chain compensates for its limited offerings by delivering a quality smash burger patty that has customers lining up on sidewalks. It doesn't say where it sources its beef, but our research points to Schweid & Sons, a family-owned and operated ground beef purveyor headquartered in Carlstadt, New Jersey.
The company sells a range of fresh and frozen beef products, including Upper ⅔ Choice Angus Beef, Certified Angus Beef, USDA Prime beef, and several varieties without any antibiotics, hormones, or steroids, such as an all-natural blend made from family farm-raised Angus. It's unclear which beef type 7th Street Burger uses for its patties, but Schweid & Sons has earned our praise before, with its Prime Burger landing on our list of favorite store-bought beef burger brands .
Texas' favorite fast-food chain maintains a steadfast commitment to freshness, offering a farm-to-table guarantee that includes the use of 100% fresh, never-frozen American beef in burgers that are made to order. According to a QSR interview with Whataburger's chief administrative officer, Alexander Ivannikov, the chain transports beef from processing plants to kitchens without the use of modified atmosphere packaging, which is typically used to slow spoilage and extend shelf life. Like In-N-Out, Whataburger ties its expansion to its beef supply chain, with plants dedicated exclusively to serving its restaurants in markets like Atlanta and Phoenix, which helps it maintain standards.
While the chain doesn't disclose where it sources beef, we did some sleuthing and dug up the name Surlean Foods. Formerly Surlean Meat Co., the San Antonio-based beef processor was founded as a sister company to L&H Packing, once one of the largest slaughterhouses in the Southwest. It has served a wide range of well-known companies over the years, including Wendy's. Whoever supplies the chain today, the fresh-beef pledge is nothing new — Whataburger has held to it since opening in 1950.
A Midwestern staple, Culver's ranks pretty high on our ranking of American burger chains . Its signature ButterBurger is composed of three cuts of beef — sirloin, chuck, and short plate – which, according to Culver's website, are sourced solely from well-marbled, filler-free, prized cuts. As to be expected, Culver's checks the "fresh, never frozen" box, and only prepares burgers to order.
The chain says that 100% of its ButterBurger beef comes from family-owned Midwestern farms, although it doesn't specify which. In a 2017 interview with The Country Today , Culver's former Chief Operating Officer, Jeff Bonner, said that the chain has worked with some beef producers for over 20 years. That certainly says something about its commitment to local farmers. Culver's is also a member of the Decade of Ag movement, which was created to develop a sustainable, climate-smart agricultural system. It has since donated more than $8 million to agricultural education via its Thank You Farmers project. Taken together, these practices show that Culver's attention to quality starts well before its beef reaches the kitchen.
Over its 24 years in business, Freddy's Frozen Custard & Steakburgers has become one of the most talked-about chains in fast food. Its signature steakburgers are cooked to order and made with 100% premium beef.
Freddy's doesn't disclose its beef supplier, but it does explain what sets a steakburger apart from a regular beef patty. Steakburgers typically use more premium cuts, such as sirloin or ribeye, sometimes blended with chuck or round. Sirloin and ribeye are both known for their beefy flavor, while chuck and round can bring a different balance of flavor and texture to the blend. Steakburgers also tend to contain more fat than traditional beef patties, and that marbling can contribute plenty of flavor. While Freddy's doesn't reveal the exact cuts in its blend, its emphasis on premium beef suggests a step up from the standard fast-food burger. Freddy's burgers are certainly worth considering if beef quality is a priority.
Unless you've spent much time in the Southeast, odds are you haven't heard of Cook Out. It's pretty ubiquitous throughout the region, and its backyard-grill-flavored burgers have helped cement it as the most popular fast food chain in North Carolina, Tennessee, and Virginia. Its Double burger is the fan-favorite, along with the butter-soaked Cajun chicken sandwich, and a legendary array of milkshake flavors.

articles.title_orig: Estonia prepares to close border with Russia after GRU-linked sabotage attacks
articles.title_zh: Estonia prepares to close border with Russia after GRU-linked sabotage attacks
articles.content_orig:
Prime Minister Kristen Michal (Reform) has requested that the "necessary steps" be taken to close Estonia's eastern border with Russia after an attempted arson attack on Saturday morning, which has been attributed to the Russian intellegence services. Road borders will close in December.
Eight Latvian citizens were detained after an attempt to break into Threod Systems' property in Viimsi, north of Tallinn, on Saturday (November 14) morning. The group was aiming to cause an explosion and set the building on fire. The company produces long-range reconnaissance and attack drones, among other things.
The Estonian Internal Security Service (KAPO) said the attack was carried out on the orders of Russia's military intelligence service, the GRU.
This is the second attempted arson attack on a defense industry company since August, when Milrem Robotics, which is based in Tallinn, was targeted.
In a statement issued on Sunday, Michal said he had discussed the possibility of closing the Estonian-Russian border with Minister of the Interior Igor Taro (Eesti 200) and had asked the minister and the Government Office to "prepare the necessary steps".
"If Russia continues its hybrid operations in Estonia, and we know that Russian intelligence services exploit border crossings to exert influence over people, we must be prepared to reduce the risks we face," he said.
On the night of 14 November, GRU-ordered sabotage attempt targeted Estonian defence company Threod Systems. Extensive damage was averted thanks to heightened security measures and a swift reaction by law enforcement. The attackers have been detained. This is part of Russia's broader hybrid war against Europe, with the aim of decreasing support to Ukraine and pressure on Russia. We will not be intimidated. Estonia is preparing for the possibility of closing its border with Russia to reduce the risks to our people and national security.
"Closing the border would reduce the threat to people in Estonia and send a clear message that attacks on Estonia's defence industry and defense capabilities are unacceptable."
The prime minister said Russia is aiming to "make us afraid, make us hesitate and weaken our support for Ukraine. Estonia's response is the opposite."
"Estonia is safe and secure. Our state institutions are vigilant, and our people and businesses know how to respond. We will not be intimidated," Michal added.
Road borders to be closed in December
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs clarified that Estonia will close road border crossing points with Russia on December 1.
Estonia has three open road border crossings with Russia in Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula, which admit pedestrians and freight goods. They operate for 12 hours a day from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
The crossing at Narva is particularly busy during summer and the New Year period, as it is one of the only land crossings with Russia still open to travelers in Europe after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Taro said the government will discuss next week closing all Estonia-Russia road border crossing points from the beginning of December.
"Estonia has already significantly restricted traffic to and from Russia at our border crossing points, warning each time that further escalation could result in a complete closure of traffic. Now that moment has arrived – following discussions with the prime minister, I will propose to the government that all Estonia-Russia road border crossing points be closed to both pedestrians and vehicles from the beginning of December," Taro said.
The government will discuss in the coming days whether the decision will be temporary or indefinite, he added.
Estonian residents and truck drivers who have traveled to Russia will be able to return home over the next two weeks.
"After that, the journey home could become long and complicated. With this step, we will further mitigate risks related to security and sanctions violations and send a message to the aggressor state that hostile actions have both consequences and a price," Taro said.
Estonia also has railway crossings with Russia in Narva and Koidula.

articles.title_orig: Three commercial vessels struck by drones near Romania's black sea, PM says
articles.title_zh: Three commercial vessels struck by drones near Romania's black sea, PM says
articles.content_orig:
Three commercial vessels were struck on Saturday evening by drones off Romania's Black Sea coast, Romanian authorities confirmed.
The drones struck the vessels near the country's Sulina canal, a key shipping route connecting the Danube river to the Black Sea and used by Ukraine to export goods.
No injuries were reported and the crews managed to extinguish the fires that broke out on board the vessels, Defence Minister Stefan Radu Oprea said.
Romanian Prime Minister Luca Niculescu called the drone attacks "unacceptable" and said it violated international law.
"They reflect the deteriorating security situation caused by Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine," he wrote on X, pledging to take necessary measures alongside its allies to strengthen security in the Black Sea.
"Romanian Ministry of Defence radars also detected aerial targets in the area," Niculescu said, adding that the Romanian Air Force had sent fighter jets on two separate occasions to investigate.
The ships that were struck included Greek-flagged chemical tanker Evia Petrol V and Saint Kitts and Nevis-flagged bulk carrier Marsol and oil products tanker Ali Najafov.
Earlier on Friday, Ukrainian media reported that another cargo vessel, the Palau-flagged Larissa 1, was hit by a drone while reportedly sailing towards Ukraine.
Russia denied targeting countries neighbouring Ukraine with drones.
Defence Minister Stefan Radu Oprea is due to meet his counterparts in Brussels next week, where the security situation in the Black Sea is expected to be discussed.
"We need the solidarity of our allies, shown through patrols with surveillance aircraft and through equipment for counter-drone warfare," Oprea said.

articles.title_orig: South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating
articles.title_zh: South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating
articles.content_orig:
A candidate who came first in South Korea's certified tax accountancy exam has admitted cheating by using a miniature camera, mobile phone and AI tools.
Han Won-seok confessed in a video on the YouTube account of his lawyer, Lee Don-Ho, adding that he had confessed to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency and offered details on how he cheated.
The 34-year-old scored 397.5 out of 400 points in the first round, getting just one of 160 questions wrong, which initially raised suspicions and sparked online speculation.
Standardised national tests play an outsized role in career trajectories for South Koreans, making their results - and efforts to unduly inflate those results - of great importance.
"I cheated in both the first and second rounds of the tax account exam by using electronic devices and generative AI," Han said in the video published on Sunday.
"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating."
When accusations he had cheated first began to surface, Han had denied any wrongdoing - but said he had changed his mind after thinking about the feelings of the candidate who had come second in the exam.
He went on to apologise to the other entrants who had passed the tests fairly.
"It seems that because of me, other successful candidates are being suspected," he suggested.
The Ministry of Employment and Labour and the Human Resources Development Service held an emergency meeting after Han admitted cheating.
The South Korean president's policy chief Ha Jun-kyung said new measures would be introduced to prevent cheating and warned "past crimes" would be "tracked down and apprehended to the very end".
Those found to have used AI to cheat in the tax accountancy exam will have their qualification revoked and will be banned from retaking the test for five years, the government said.
The scandal comes just days before the east Asian nation's annual college entrance exam, a crucial hurdle for students.
Han said he had only cheated to try and earn money and get a job that would make his parents proud of him again.
Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency told Korean news agency Yonhap on Sunday that it was looking into the case.
"We received a written confession through the test taker's lawyer this morning regarding cheating on the tax accountant exam," it confirmed in a statement.
It added that the case had now been assigned to investigators.
Because of the significance of the national exams, instances of cheating are not uncommon in South Korea, and cases involving the use of AI have become more prominent as the technology becomes more sophisticated.
Last month, two college applicants were reported to have used AI glasses to try and cheat their entrance exams at two Seoul universities.
Education ministry data also says there were four cases of cheating through AI glasses at middle and high schools in the past 12 months.

articles.title_zh: Yemeni government force retreats from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
articles.content_orig:
Forces backed by Saudi Arabia in Yemen said on Sunday that they were withdrawing from the country’s Red Sea coast, where they have been fighting for weeks to retake strategic territory from the Iran-aligned Houthi militia.
A group of fighters called the Southern Armed Forces, who are allied with the government of Yemen, said in a statement that they were “redeploying” to protect the interim capital, Aden, citing recent battlefield developments and “threats targeting” the city.
Aden has been the seat of the internationally recognized government for more than a decade, since the Houthis seized control of Sanaa, the Yemeni capital.
The retreat is a blow for the Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia as the balance of power in Yemen continues to tilt toward the Houthis, analysts said.
“The Houthis are very determined to go to Aden,” said Ahmed Nagi, a senior analyst for Yemen at the International Crisis Group. “They don’t want to see any area controlled by the government or the Saudi side, so they want to take over everything at this moment.”

articles.title_orig: Romania slams ‘unacceptable’ drone strikes on Black Sea ships
articles.title_zh: Romania slams ‘unacceptable’ drone strikes on Black Sea ships
articles.content_orig:
Romanian Prime Minister Luca Niculescu on Sunday condemned drone strikes on three commercial ships near his country's Black Sea coast, promising to work with NATO allies to strengthen security in the region following the latest attacks.
“These incidents are unacceptable and constitute a violation of international law,” Niculescu said in a post on X. He added that Russia's war against Ukraine was causing the security situation in the Black Sea to deteriorate.
The ships were hit Saturday evening and overnight near Sulina, a Romanian port where the Danube River meets the Black Sea.
The Greek-flagged oil tanker Evia Petrol V was struck just after 9 p.m., followed 35 minutes later by a strike on another ship, the Marsol, according to a statement from Romania's defense ministry published on its Facebook page.
“In both cases, the fires were extinguished by the ships' crews. No casualties were reported,” the ministry said.
A third vessel, the Ali Najafov, also reported being struck overnight. It remains unclear who launched the drones.
Romania's military detected aerial targets on radar and sent F-16 fighter jets into the air. Authorities also issued warnings to residents near the coast about possible drone threats.
The attacks came after another commercial ship, the Larissa 1, was reportedly hit by a drone near Romania's coast on Friday.
Romanian Defense Minister Ștefan-Radu Oprea said Sunday he would raise the incidents with allied counterparts in Brussels. “We need the solidarity of our allies,” he said, calling for more surveillance aircraft and equipment to defend against drones.
Last week, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced the EU will help finance some Black Sea security costs following recent attacks on commercial shipping.
In October, at least seven commercial vessels were struck by drones in the Black Sea close to NATO and EU members Romania and Bulgaria, leaving more than 20 sailors dead and dozens missing.

articles.title_orig: Supermarket badly damaged as thieves rip cash machine from wall
articles.title_zh: Supermarket badly damaged as thieves rip cash machine from wall
articles.content_orig:
Thieves have ripped a cash machine out of the wall of a supermarket near Stirling, leaving the building badly damaged.
Police were alerted to the theft at the Co-op in Doune at about 03:30 and later found the ATM in a pick-up truck at a premises off the B826.
Part of the shop's wall has collapsed, leaving the inside completely exposed and the pavement strewn with debris.
It has been cordoned off by officers and Castlehill is closed to vehicles and pedestrians while the building is assessed.
It follows a spate of ATM thefts in other parts of Scotland.
In September, two cash machines were torn out of the walls of a bank on Peebles High Street and taken away on a horsebox.
A telescopic forklift, used to ram the building, was left abandoned in the street.
Days earlier, a truck was rammed into a Co-op in West Calder in an attempt to steal the ATM.
Det Insp Chris Carson said inquiries into the latest theft were ongoing.
He urged anyone who witnessed the incident, or who has relevant dashcam or CCTV footage, to get in touch .

articles.title_orig: 5 Generations Of The Chevy Impala SS Ranked From Best To Worst Horsepower Ratings
articles.title_zh: 5 Generations Of The Chevy Impala SS Ranked From Best To Worst Horsepower Ratings
articles.content_orig:
Mention a Chevy Impala, and thoughts of an unremarkable family sedan may come to mind, but add an SS next to the nameplate and things change. The Impala SS (Super Sport) is a pure horsepower play that dates back to 1961, two years after the Bowtie brand launched the Impala as a standalone model. Its numbers are still impressive, even by 21st-century standards. The retail version of the Impala SS from the 1960s, which covered two generations, produced up to 425 horsepower. The later Impala SS generations from the 1990s and 2000s were less brutish, offering between 240 and 303 hp, but they were still a step up from their more mundane counterparts.
However, these horsepower numbers come with a catch. The output figures for 1960s Impala SS models reflected gross horsepower ratings, which generally didn't account for intake, exhaust, and accessory loads. When the 1970s rolled around, the auto industry was dealing with tighter emissions regulations and insurance companies that took a dim view of high-powered cars. By the 1972 model year, Detroit switched to net horsepower calculations to better reflect real-world engine configurations. Because gross horsepower ratings often varied from manufacturer to manufacturer, there's no standard way to convert horsepower ratings between the methods, but both still measure horsepower at the crankshaft, not the wheels.
Our ranking of every Impala SS generation by power takes into account the highest advertised horsepower ratings for regular-production SS models, regardless of whether it's gross or net. Special race versions and modified cars are excluded. Here's how every Impala SS generation compares in maximum power output.
The first Impala was a variant of the 1958 Bel Air, but the SS designation didn't arrive until the third-generation Impala in 1961. The second generation, without a Super Sport option, filled the two-year gap as the free-standing Impala model. The first Impala SS model's power output is a story of progression. The 1961 Impala SS arrived with a choice of V8 engines: 348-cubic-inch units rated at 305, 340, or 350 horsepower and a 409-cubic-inch V8 officially rated at 360 horsepower. In 1962, that king-of-the-hill powerplant could also be configured with dual four-barrel carburetors, increasing output to 409 horsepower.
Thanks to solid lifters, dual exhausts, and an 11:1 compression ratio, the 409's output rose to 425 gross horsepower for the 1963 model year. Chevy history buffs may also recall a 1963 Z11 lightweight drag-racing Impala with a 430-horsepower 427-cubic-inch V8. Keep in mind that this one wasn't a Super Sport model, nor was it a part of regular production, as only 57 were ever produced. The 1964 Impala SS continued with the same 409 from the previous year.
Horsepower for the second iteration of the Impala SS was in familiar territory, with peak outputs sitting at 425, but the Impala eventually took a different route to get there. To start, Chevy launched an entirely new Impala with a sleeker exterior and a perimeter frame, ditching the X-type architecture of the outgoing model. The new looks helped the 1965 Impala become the best-selling single model of all time. A record 1,046,514 units were sold, with roughly 23% being SS variants. Impala SS examples from this generation still attract a lot of attention online .
The top engine for the non-SS 1965 Impala was the familiar Turbo-Fire 409-cubic-inch V8, making 400 horsepower. For the SS, Chevy also offered the L78 V8, a 396-cubic-inch V8 rated at 425 gross horsepower. A year later, the L72 427-cubic-inch V8 joined the options list, also rated for up to 425 hp. The powerplant featured a forged crankshaft and pistons, solid lifters, and a dual exhaust system. The SS 427 continued into 1967 and 1968, but with a slightly different L36 engine, still with 427 cubic inches, but now rated at 385 hp. In 1969, output increased to 390 hp.
The final Impala SS came with 303 hp, which is the most of any modern generation. The supercharged V6 in the previous eighth-generation SS was replaced with a naturally aspirated 5.3-liter LS4 V8. That results in a zero-to-60 mph dash of 5.6 seconds, which is on par with a modern-day Mazda Miata – but remember, this was 20 years ago.
That seems straightforward enough, but the final-generation Impala SS has some quirks that don't match its muscle-era badge. Notably, the ninth-generation Impala was front-wheel-drive, and naturally, so was the SS variant. Power traveled through a four-speed automatic transmission, albeit a heavy-duty version. Despite having an upgraded suspension that helped this SS go beyond a rental car-spec version, reviews of the day weren't particularly kind to the SS. In a 2006 road test, Car and Driver stated, "The SS seems to have been created to produce impressive numbers on paper with little regard to driver enjoyment." Nonetheless, the Impala SS's swan song continued through the 2009 model year.
After a quarter-century hiatus, Chevrolet resurrected the Impala SS for the 1994 model year. This time, it was packaged in a rear-wheel-drive sedan with a 260-horsepower 5.7-liter V8 engine under the hood. Engineers didn't have to dig too far into the parts bin. This LT1 V8 already saw duty in the Camaro and Corvette, although there are different LT1 versions over the years . However, the engine in the Impala SS was modified with cast-iron cylinder heads and a different camshaft. It was also tuned for more torque: 330 pound-feet in this application. By today's standards, a 0-to-60 mph dash of seven seconds is nothing exciting, but this was three decades ago, and this Impala SS weighed about 4,300 pounds.
That bulk came from the full-sized Caprice, which underpinned this seventh-generation version. In effect, you could say that Chevrolet made a civilian version of the Caprice police car. The vehicle included an upgraded suspension, improved cooling, larger disc brakes, and a limited-slip differential. The five-spoke aluminum wheels and subtle strips of exterior chrome trim helped distinguish this Impala from its workhorse siblings. Leather upholstery was another clue. For its final production year, 1996, the column-mounted shifter was moved to the center console, and a tachometer was added. That's why low-mileage 1996 Impala SS examples still hold strong collector appeal.
The short-lived eighth-generation Impala SS (2004–2005) stands out for a couple of reasons besides having the lowest engine output (240 horsepower). Namely, it's the only Impala SS with a V6 engine. Yet this is no ordinary six-cylinder powerplant; it's General Motors' 3.8-liter Series II engine with an Eaton supercharger, known for its broad torque band.
This Impala SS is based on the eighth-generation Impala, which was introduced for the 2000 model year as a front-wheel-drive sedan. Fast forward to 2004, and Chevrolet added the SS variant to the lineup, marking the first Impala SS that spins the front wheels. An upgraded four-speed automatic transmission controls the setup, but this Chevy also has larger anti-roll bars, modified springs, and Goodyear performance tires. As a result, 0-60 mph came in 6.5 seconds.
To go beyond a plain-Jane Impala, the automaker also added four round taillights (marketing language called this a Corvette-inspired treatment), black-only exterior paint, a small rear spoiler, leather upholstery, and a slathering of SS badges inside and out. This Impala was axed after 2005 to make way for the aforementioned 2006 Impala SS with a more powerful V8 engine.

articles.title_orig: ‘It is not unusual to go 48 hours with little sleep’: what it’s like to cover a Cop climate summit
articles.title_zh: ‘It is not unusual to go 48 hours with little sleep’: what it’s like to cover a Cop climate summit
articles.content_orig:
The UN’s annual climate conference began in Turkey this week. Reporting from the event can be gruelling work – but it’s also crucial.
T hey are counting on you not to read our coverage of the Cop31 climate talks. Fossil fuel companies, climate science deniers, petrostates, far right populists … They want you to think the negotiations are too intractable, the progress too halting, the issues too complex, too tortuous, too pointless, TL;DR.
But as the UN’s 31st annual climate conference got underway in Antalya, Turkey this week, our journalists have been going to great lengths to help you understand why the talks remain urgent , crucial and – hopefully – consequential. As well as helping you follow the agreements reached and progress made during the two week summit, they have also been highlighting what’s at stake .
Covering a Cop is gruelling work. The negotiations are by definition difficult: representatives from almost every country in the world attempt to thrash out consensus agreements and roadmaps for confronting humanity’s greatest threat. There are also practical hurdles, with 70,000 registered delegates at this year’s summit, packed venues and tangled schedules. On Tuesday morning , the Guardian’s live blog from the conference also chronicled the odyssey of our journalist Graham Readfearn as he struggled for three and a half hours just to get to the venue on one of the special Cop31 buses that got caught in the Antalya traffic.
Graham’s quest wasn’t a metaphor – it was just one of many practical challenges reporters face when covering a Cop (which stands for Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change). These challenges are that much harder for smaller media organisations from poorer nations that are particularly vulnerable to the impacts of the climate emergency.
I asked some of our journalists ​why it’s such an important conference to cover and the challenges they face reporting from it.
Ajit Niranjan European environment correspondent
“The hardest thing about covering Cop is satisfying the many different audiences who turn to our coverage during this chaotic fortnight. For the tens of thousands of people attending the summit, we offer a close-up view of the diplomatic spats (and rare breakthroughs) that have sweeping consequences for humanity and the other species with which we share this planet. And for the average Guardian reader, who cares about the climate but may not need the minutiae of UN diplomacy, we mix key takeaways from the negotiations with the most riveting, heartbreaking, terrifying and encouraging stories about the climate crisis. It’s a rare moment during the year when climate change is in the spotlight, and we want to serve as many readers as we can.”
Adam Morton Executive editor, news, politics and sport, Guardian Australia, and previously climate and environment editor
“Getting across a summit that can draw 100,000 people to attend countless events and backroom meetings is challenging enough, but perhaps the hardest thing about covering Cop is working through the exhaustion that hits after two weeks of long days chasing ministers and bureaucrats across a vast convention centre as they haggle over acronyms that are impenetrable to normal people. By the end of the final weekend it is not unusual to have gone 48 hours with little to no sleep, as delegates work through the night, well past the scheduled deadline, to try to reach an agreement. Power naps on any available surface can become a necessity. Covering a Cop is a great reporting assignment - sometimes deeply frustrating, sometimes exhilarating - but the exercise of being present and alert to translate what the end result means in tangible terms for readers across the globe is an endurance test.”
Fiona Harvey Environment editor
“The annual Cop summits might seem futile, and they certainly have long stretches of tedium. Logistically, they’re a nightmare, as tens of thousands of delegates descend on a new location each year to spend a fortnight in white air-conditioned conference halls and cramped negotiating rooms. Oh, and the food is always terrible.
Every day at a Cop is a flurry of text messages, emails, calls, sprints down corridors desperately trying to doorstep world leaders, and forlorn attempts to update yourself on which press conferences have been cancelled, which meetings rearranged, what rumours have been scotched and which of those flying about might still be true.
On the futility side, it’s true that after three decades of Cops the climate crisis has not gone away, and global greenhouse gas emissions have continued to rise. But that’s not the whole story. The world is moving away from fossil fuels, albeit far too slowly, and those impeding that progress need to be held to account. In many countries, voters can do that, but a huge slice of the world’s emissions and fossil fuel production come from autocratic states where elections are not free and fair. Cop is one of the few places where those countries can be questioned and exposed on their failings and attempts at obstruction. Cops are also, at their best, engines for progress - countries encourage each other to do the right thing. As John Kerry [the former US secretary of state] told me, just ahead of Cop31 , when I asked him whether Cops were worth it: ‘I’d rather have it [Cop] taking place, and having people listen to each other and exchange information and views, than live in a completely dark, motionless pit where nothing happens.’”
Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent, Guardian Australia
“I can’t pick the one thing that’s hardest. They are sprawling in scale, cut across geopolitics, science, diplomacy, social affairs and so many other big issues. I’m based in Australia, so there’s always a long flight to take and some jet lag to deal with while at the same time trying to be on top of your game from day one. It’s exhausting, relentless and exhilarating. If none of my colleagues have mentioned the acronyms, then TBH they should have. You need to know your LDCs from your NDCs and your HACs from your WEOGs. The big challenge is to know enough to then be able to translate what’s happening into a language the reader understands, and to be able to tell the difference between a development that’s genuinely going to be consequential and something that’s just part of the Cop noise. And I never eat or sleep properly.”
Damien Gayle Environment correspondent
“The most challenging thing about covering Cop is cutting through the forests of jargon to find your way to the story that actually means something to the outside world. It’s all too easy to get caught up with the excitement of Cop. For two weeks it is like a world in itself – part summit, part trade fair, part festival. Those participating believe it is the most important place anywhere, and that the fate of the world hangs on every intricacy. And it is important. But it still needs to be kept in perspective.”

articles.title_zh: Europe needs to talk to Russia
articles.content_orig:
Europe’s
security is impossible without Ukraine that is integrated into the regional
institutions, Polish columnist Edwin Bendyk said on Nov. 12.
He made the comments during a panel discussion titled ‘Why
Poland Needs Ukraine and Ukraine Needs Poland’ at the Re:Open Zakarpattia 2026
forum.
For Ukraine to successfully serve as a security guarantor
for Europe, it must be economically successful and politically integrated,
Bendyk said. At the same time, he specified that this does not mean Ukraine
should be given special treatment.
But security should be the top priority, he said, adding
that economic disputes, including those over grain, must be resolved.
Bendyk recalled that in 1991, Poland’s political elites
decided to support Ukraine’s independence despite public opposition. He called
for a similar effort to establish a list of priorities today.
According to Bendyk, France has radically changed its
strategic assessment of Russia and no longer has doubts that Russia will pose a
threat in the future.
Bendyk acknowledged that Poland had long viewed the United
States as an unwavering pillar of its security but has now found that this is
no longer the case. As recently as last year, he said, Poland was convinced
that its security system should rely on NATO and the United States.
Now, he said, there is a belief that Poland, Ukraine, and the
EU can form a strong enough alliance to stand up to Russia.
Bendyk said people should not listen to either Russian or U.S.
propaganda about a “weak Europe.” Europe is technologically and militarily
strong; “it just does not know it yet,” he said.
He also stressed that Poland’s strategic support and
military aid for Ukraine remain unchanged and that no political or historical
disputes will alter them.
The military war may be swinging in our favor, but the information war continues.
Just as an army needs soldiers, so does a free society need its journalists to ensure that people have access to honest, trustworthy voices to understand the world around them.
For the past five years, The New Voice of Ukraine has been working tirelessly to push back against Russian narratives and defend democracy. But we cannot do it alone.

articles.title_orig: FDA rejects Summit’s ivonescimab, derailing US arrival of much-hyped PD-1xVEGF class
articles.title_zh: FDA rejects Summit’s ivonescimab, derailing US arrival of much-hyped PD-1xVEGF class
articles.content_orig:
The immuno-oncology revolution will have to wait.
The FDA has issued a complete response letter to Summit Therapeutics, declining to approve the highly anticipated PD-1xVEGF bispecific ivonescimab for patients with previously treated, EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer.
The rejection derails the immediate U.S. launch of a drug class that many industry heavyweights believe could eventually dethrone Merck & Co.’s Keytruda.
Summit’s initial application targeted a niche, and as Leerink Partners analysts pointed out in a Nov. 5 note, the limitations of the clinical trial behind the application are not directly transferable to Summit’s broader development program for ivonescimab.
To industry watchers, the regulatory snub does not come as a total surprise. In their Nov. 5 note, Leerink analysts assigned Summit’s bid a 40% probability to approval. That’s because the phase 3 Harmoni trial underpinning Summit’s application failed to meet its overall survival (OS) endpoint, even as the FDA specifically demanded a statistically significant death reduction.
At the primary overall survival analysis of the global Harmoni trial last year, the OS hazard ratio was 0.98 in the Western subgroup, indicating no survival benefit for ivonescimab plus chemotherapy versus chemo alone at that time. Summit argued that the OS data in the Western cohort was too immature compared to the China cohort, and subsequent data cuts showed that Western results improved to 0.76 by June 2026, matching the result from the entire trial. The FDA, however, apparently decided to stick with its OS requirement.
In the CRL, the FDA noted that, without a statistically significant OS improvement, Summit has not established substantial evidence of effectiveness, and that a progression-free survival (PFS) benefit in the absence of a statistically significant OS does not support a positive benefit-risk profile in support of approval, according to Summit.
“We are disappointed for patients and their families awaiting additional treatment options in this setting,” Robert Duggan, chairman and co-CEO of Summit said in a Nov. 15 release.
Before FDA handed out the rejection, Summit had parted ways with its chief commercial officer Robert LaCaze and several senior commercial and marketing leaders who were tasked with building ivonescimab’s launch plan.
Meanwhile, back in China, where ivonescimab’s original developer, Akeso, is in charge, authorities granted the drug its first approval in May 2024 in the same indication of tyrosine kinase inhibitor-pretreated EGFR-mutated nonsquamous NSCLC. Then, the China-only Harmoni-A trial, part of which was merged into the global Harmoni trial, met its OS endpoint at the final analysis with a 26% death risk reduction.
Ivonescimab’s setback has narrowed its potential first-mover advantage as several pharma giants— including Merck —race to advance their own PD-(L)1xVEGF bispecifics.
Pfizer’s 3SBio-partnered tivunatamig (PF-08634404), BioNTech and Bristol Myers Squibb’s pumitamig , Merck’s MK-2010 and AbbVie’s ABBV-1480 are all getting pushed into global phase 3 trials.
Even in the second-line EGFR-mutated NSCLC space, ivonescimab’s absence means one less competitor for TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugates such as AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo’s Datroway and Merck’s Kelun-Biotech-partnered sac-TMT , as well as BMS’ dual-targeting EGFRxHER3 bispecific ADC, iza-bren .
Now, attention around the PD-(L)1xVEGF class is shifting to the all-important first-line NSCLC setting. As Leerink’s analysts noted, the real test for ivonescimab remains the upcoming readout from the Harmoni-3 trial in first-line NSCLC.
Summit scared investors in April, when a newly added interim analysis of the trial’s squamous cohort missed statistical significance on PFS. The squamous subgroup is now moving toward a final PFS analysis by the end of this year, and the nonsquamous group could report PFS data in the first half of 2027.
Despite the regulatory sting, Summit is far from defeated. Just weeks before the FDA’s decision, the biotech secured a $2 billion cash injection from AZ.
The company now has the financial firepower to fund additional trials for ivonescimab, and AZ plans to pair its sprawling ADC pipeline with the PD-1xVEGF drug, an approach that some considered the next-frontier in immuno-oncology.
“With five positive Phase III studies between Summit and Akeso, nothing changes with respect to our ever-growing belief in the opportunity for ivonescimab and our determination to advance ivonescimab’s development,” Duggan said. “Our mission remains to improve outcomes for patients facing significant unmet needs, which is work worth doing, and we will continue through our expansive clinical development program.”

articles.title_zh: How Nvidia's scandal knocked thousands off your 401(k)
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Jensen Huang, who co-founded Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) over three decades ago at a Denny's restaurant, is officially out as CEO of the artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant .
Multiple reports about multiple alleged extramarital affairs Huang had, one with a woman who may have been a Chinese spy and others with as many as two Nvidia employees, quickly led the torchbearer of AI to resign.
Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »
CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. Nvidia stock has sunk over 28% in the past month.
While Huang is undoubtedly the most important CEO in AI, his departure is unlikely to slow down the sector, and Nvidia is likely to press on as the dominant chip player. But that doesn't mean Nvidia is in the clear. Forget Huang -- this is the real question investors need to ask about Nvidia stock.
Jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.
There's no denying Huang's importance to Nvidia -- his leadership may have even commanded a premium for the stock.
But at the end of the day, Nvidia will still have the same graphics processing units (GPUs) that have significantly outperformed their competition. I guess one could argue that future innovation might not be as secure as it was, but I don't think anyone can say that definitively.
Nvidia has maintained a moat since 2006 through its CUDA programming platform, on which most software developers have been trained, which makes switching to a new system difficult. That advantage won't go away.
When it comes to the stock and the financials driving it, the real question investors need to ask concerns Nvidia's relationship with the Singaporean data center Megaspeed, which reportedly led to illegal chip sales. The alleged Chinese spy with whom Huang reportedly had an affair, Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen), was a top executive at Megaspeed.
Tech news site The Information reported this week that over $7 billion of chip sales from Nvidia to Megaspeed eventually made their way to China illegally.
Nvidia has not been able to sell chips to China since April 2025, when the U.S. government said it would require the company to obtain an export license. Since then, Chinese sales have been virtually zero, according to the company. Nvidia and Huang have lobbied President Donald Trump's administration to restart sales in the region. But even before then, Nvidia could sell only older-generation chips due to national security concerns.
What investors are likely wondering is whether Nvidia's relationship with Megaspeed is a one-off, or whether more of Nvidia's previous revenue has derived from similar relationships.
Interestingly, the independent short-seller Culper Research went short Nvidia in May of this year, betting that more of Nvidia's sales have a similar dynamic.
"We believe that in reality, over 20% of Nvidia's FY 2026 compute revenues remained driven by China via illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries," Culper wrote on X in May.
More incredibly, Culper specifically called out Megaspeed and said it had uncovered documents showing the company had been financed by the Chinese tech giant Alibaba through a Singaporean shell company.
If Culper's thesis, which looks a lot more plausible now, is true, that could mean real trouble for Nvidia's revenue and earnings.
While it looked like Nvidia was about to sell chips to China again in the near future, this whole matter could prompt the Trump administration to revisit export restrictions and potentially make them even stricter. Nvidia may also face tougher standards when selling chips abroad to prove they are not being illegally diverted. This could prove costly.
Now, it's also possible that Culper is wrong and the chip giant is still allowed to resume sales of chips to Chinese companies.
Ultimately, while Huang is the big headline, the bigger questions are whether a material amount of Nvidia's current and prior chip sales is being illegally diverted to China and whether Nvidia can resume sales to Chinese companies in the future.

articles.title_orig: PlayStation 4 can now run 9B AI model on its GCN GPU at up to 39 tokens per second
articles.title_zh: PlayStation 4 can now run 9B AI model on its GCN GPU at up to 39 tokens per second
articles.content_orig:
Garlic LLM uses custom GPU kernels and 3-bit and 4-bit quantization to run a 9B AI model on PS4.
As you know, we don’t usually cover AI model releases. We believe GPUs are better suited for gaming and rendering, but some projects still catch our interest. One example is a developer who managed to run a 9-billion-parameter AI model on the original PlayStation 4 using its AMD GCN GPU.
The project, called Garlic LLM, runs Qwen3.5-9B entirely offline, without Linux or an external computer. Developer Leonardo Alegría contacted VideoCardz to share details of the open-source application, which reportedly achieves 31 to 39 tokens per second on Sony’s 2013 console. To be honest, I didn’t even realize such an old hardware can still run modern AI models.
The PS4 was never designed to run modern language models, and its homebrew environment lacks a dedicated GPU compute API or machine-learning libraries. To overcome this limitation, Alegría developed custom GPU kernels using OpenCL C and compiled them for AMD’s GCN architecture. The application communicates directly with the GPU through hand-written PM4 command buffers rather than relying on a conventional graphics driver.
Memory capacity was another limitation. The PS4 has 8GB of shared GDDR5 memory, so Garlic LLM uses custom quantization to fit Qwen3.5-9B into approximately 4.5 GiB. Most model weights use 4-bit precision, while the larger MLP gate and up projection matrices use 3-bit quantization. The KV cache also uses 4-bit precision, allowing the application to support a 16K-token context window.
The developer also implemented speculative decoding using Qwen3.5’s built-in Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) head. This allows the model to predict up to two tokens ahead and verify them in a single pass. According to Alegría, the technique increased generation performance from approximately 22 tokens per second to 31–39 tokens per second, reaching up to 43 tokens per second when generating code. Usually that’s considered usuable for daily use.
I would argue that a 9B model has limited use beyond basic chat and tool calling. This particular Qwen model isn’t that good at coding, and the project is limited to a 16K context window, which isn’t much by today’s standards. Still, we’re talking about hardware from 2013 that was never designed to run AI models in the first place.

articles.content_orig:
Published: 06:12 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 11:18 EST, 15 November 2026
Almost 1,500 migrants arrived in the Canary Islands on Saturday as Spain 's crisis continues to spiral.
A total of 2,200 people on 14 boats travelled to the islands over the weekend by the Spanish coastguards in the region, where thousands of Britons flock each year on holiday.
The Maritime Rescue Service said 1,324 had been rescued - a figure close to the daily record for that route. In November 2020, 1,461 people were recorded to have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands.
It marked the highest number of migrants to have made the crossing on a single day in six years, when 1,461 people were rescued in waters off the islands in November 2020.
A single boat rescued on Saturday was carrying some 240 people, including 12 women and 36 children, according to local authorities.
Those rescued – most of whom were from Senegal, Gambia and Guinea Conakry – were taken to El Hierro, a small island which declared a state of emergency last week following a surge in migrant arrivals.
Twelve boats arrived on the island, while one other was taken to Gran Canaria and a further vessel in Tenerife.
The Atlantic route from West Africa to the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration crossings.
Thousands attempt the journey each year in overcrowded boats, seeking to reach Spanish territory despite rough seas, strong currents and long distances.
The Spanish Maritime Rescue Service is seen helping immigrants off a wooden boat near El Hierro in the Canary Islands on Saturday
A total of 1,488 people travelling on 14 boats were rescued by the Spanish coastguards this weekend... a boat is pictured off the coast of El Hierro earlier this week
Migrants are seen lined up overnight at the port of La Restinga, El Hierro, on Saturday
Thousands of Britons flock to the Canary Islands on holiday every year
Arrivals tend to pick up in the autumn months, when sea conditions along the route are generally calmer and more favourable for crossings.
Spain's Territorial Policy Minister Angel Victor Torres is set to visit El Hierro on Sunday to discuss the surge in migrant arrivals.
More than 5,000 illegal migrants have arrived on the island, home to approximately 12,000 people, this month alone.
Maritime services in El Hierro said they rescued 3,261 migrants in the first six days of November, with regional authorities warning on Friday the numbers were 'absolutely unsustainable'.
As of Monday, Spanish outlets reported that the figure was nearing 5,000 after ten more small boats carrying hundreds of people arrived on the island over the weekend.
Earlier this week, a spokesman for the island's Unified Police Union said authorities were 'overwhelmed' and struggling to cope with the number of arrivals, warning, 'we are experiencing a situation similar to the one... in Ceuta, out of control and overwhelming.'
Alpidio Armas, head of El Hierro's governing council, told Spanish television over the weekend: 'We are very concerned... by this sharp increase in arrivals.'
'This is precisely what has led us to declare an emergency in order to ensure a framework of cooperation with higher-level institutions.'
At least nine migrants have died off Spain's Canary Islands, and a critically ill baby was airlifted to hospital upon arrival in recent weeks, while thousands of other people have been rescued.
Following the border rush into Ceuta in July, the Spanish government has been facing mounting pressure over its handling of the migration crisis.
While the national government says around 5,000 migrants remain in the enclave, Ceuta's mayor says up to 15,000 remain.
Local authorities also accuse the government of ignoring warning signs before the border was breached.
Many migrants in Ceuta, including unaccompanied minors, remain sleeping in the streets despite authorities' efforts to shelter, register and deport those who are eligible back to Morocco.
